title: Characterization of biofilms on extracorporeal life support system (ECLS) cannulae and their relevance to bacteremia or fungemia.
summary:
Extracorporeal life support systems (ECLS) are established standard for patients with severe lung failure or cardiovascular failure. For this therapy, two large cannulars are inserted into the patient’s vascular system. Bacteria can deposit on the surfaces of the cannulas and form biofilms. These can then become the starting point for severe infections or sepsis.
In this study, we would like to examine the cannulas for biofilms after removal from the patient using microbiological culture and NGS. We would also like to examine the patient's blood by blood culture and NGS shortly after pulling the cannulas. The findings should then be compared with previous and subsequent microbiological findings.

interventions.name: Collections of data and examinations are performed on the day of ECLS decannulation.
